items.evidence: The acceptance AC#1 test passes. It asserts handsDealt 10, voluntary 5, preflopRaised 2, vpip 50, pfr 20, '50%' and '20%'. The fixture has an SB completion (small-blind then call), a BB check (big-blind then check, board 3) and 4 preflop folds, one of them after posting the SB. Mutants that make check voluntary, drop call from VPIP, make blinds voluntary or count calls as PFR are all killed. Holdout fixtures: SB completion → voluntary 1. BB check → voluntary 0 and sees flop/showdown. Raise then fold to a 3-bet, and repeated 3-bets → voluntary/PFR count once per hand. All match.

The AC#2 test passes with postflopAggressive 4, postflopCalls 4, preflopRaised 2 and aggression 50 ('50%'), across flop, turn and river, with checks and a fold present. Mutants that include preflop or count checks as passive are killed. Holdout: a multiway muck hand gives bet 1 / calls 2 and raise+bet = 2 aggressive. A river bet with a fold-out gives 1 aggressive. Across 70,000 real hands (seed 42 cash Mixed 25k, seed 7 cash 25k, seed 1234 sng 20k), per-seat postflopAggressive/postflopCalls equal my own counter exactly.

The AC#3 test passes with sawFlop 8, showdowns 2 and wtsd 25, and includes preflop folds with a board of 3 that are not counted as flops. Mutants for sawFlop ignoring preflop fold, requiring a flop action, or using any fold are killed. Holdout: a preflop fold with a board of 5 → sawFlop 0, showdown 0. A turn/flop fold while others reach showdown → sawFlop 1, showdowns 0. Real hands: sawFlop and showdowns match my counter for every seat on all three runs (e.g. seed 42 seat 1: 3650 / 3455).

The AC#4 test passes with showdowns 2, showdownsWon 1, wsd 50 and '50%', where the won hand is a split with both winners amount 5. The sole-winner-only mutant is killed. Holdout: both split seats count as won. A zero-amount winner entry is not won. Real hands: showdownsWon matches exactly. A second oracle from chip movement (final stack − starting stack + contribution − returned) agreed with award totals for every seat in every hand (342+429+490 split hands covered).

The AC#5 test passes: (a) all five are null and show '—'; (b) wtsd and wsd are null and vpip/pfr are numbers; (c) only wsd is null; (d) aggression is null and the rest are numbers. AC#5(b) correction judged on substance: a seat that never saw a flop can have no postflop actions, so aggression must also be null. The spec's wording that the 'other stats' are numbers is literally impossible for aggression in (b). The test asserts the correct behaviour. Holdout: styleStats(EMPTY) is all null. No-flop, no-showdown and checks-only cases give the expected nulls and numbers. formatStat(null) is U+2014 and NO_STAT is U+2014. The null→0 mutant is killed.
The AC#6 test passes: BB folding to a raise and SB folding → handsDealt 2, voluntary 0, vpip 0, '0%' (not '—'). Holdout: SB fold and BB fold to a raise both give all-zero counts except handsDealt 1.

The unit edge-hands test passes and covers (a)–(f) as specified. Holdout fixtures match. Preflop all-in raise plus runout (board 5, no flop actions) → voluntary, PFR, sawFlop and showdown, and the caller wins. An all-in BB that never acts → not voluntary but sawFlop/showdown 1. Mucked loser (absent from result.showdown) → showdown 1, not won. Returned-only seat → not won. Side-pot-only winner and short all-in main-pot winner → won, while the side-pot loser is not. River bet with fold-out → no showdown, 1 aggressive. Real hands exercised 6387+8285+7030 mucked showdown seats, 150 all-in runout seats and 68 multi-pot hands with zero mismatches.

The unit test passes: undealt seat 9 equals EMPTY_STYLE_COUNTS (frozen). addStyleCounts is checked field by field with distinct values. styleCounts equals the fold. Empty input → EMPTY. Inputs are deep-equal to a structuredClone. Formats are 33%, 0% and 100%. Holdout: the undealt seat is all zeros, deep-frozen inputs do not throw, a generator iterable is accepted, and addStyleCounts does not mutate. formatStat gives 200/3→'67%', 12.5→'13%', 0.4→'0%' and 99.6→'100%'. The sng run (seats eliminated, e.g. seat 6 dealt 4218/20000) matched my counter for undealt seats too.

The unit test passes in 528 ms standalone (seed 42, 300 hands, 6 seats). It asserts the invariants, the handsDealt sum equal to the sum of record.seats.length, at least 2 showdowns and at least 1 won per showdown hand, and 0 showdowns per fold-out. Mutants for showdown-ignores-folds and won-without-showdown are killed. My own 70,000-hand cross-check of all 8 counts for all 6 seats on 3 seeds and both game types found 0 per-hand mismatches, equal totals, and 0 disagreements between fold records and the engine's player.folded flag.
The unit test passes a typed CompletedHand fixture straight to handStyleCounts and asserts the full counts. npm run typecheck exits 0, so CompletedHand is assignable to StatHand with no adapter.

findings.expected_vs_actual: Expected: the tests pin formatStat to whole-percent rounding (Math.round), as the spec says. Actual: the module rounds correctly (200/3 → '67%', 12.5 → '13%'), but every formatted value the tests check is a whole number or rounds down (33.3→33%). A formatStat that truncates instead of rounding would still pass the suite.
findings.fix: Non-blocking: add a formatStat case whose fraction rounds up (for example 200/3 → '67%') so truncation fails a test.

findings.expected_vs_actual: Expected (spec text for AC#5(b)): the stats other than wtsd and wsd are numbers. Actual: aggression is null when the seat never saw a flop. This is the only correct result, because there are no postflop actions, and the test asserts it. The spec sentence is wrong, not the code.
findings.fix: Non-blocking: when the spec or story doc is next touched, reword AC#5(b) so aggression is also '—' when no flop was seen.
